question: Which among the following is an extra-constitutional body? (RRB JE (26/05/2019) Shift 2 CBT 1)
options: Language Commission
Election Commission
Finance Commission
Planning Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Planning Commission

Explanation:
In India, constitutional bodies are those explicitly mentioned in the Constitution, such as the Election Commission (Article 324), Finance Commission (Article 280), and Language Commission (Article 344). The Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional body, established in 1950 via a cabinet resolution, not under any constitutional provision. Its primary role was to formulate five-year plans for economic development. In 2014, it was replaced by the NITI Aayog, which is also an extra-constitutional body. Hence, the correct answer is Planning Commission.

☛ When was Planning Commission formed? → 1950.
☛ Which body replaced Planning Commission? → NITI Aayog (2015).
☛ What type of body is NITI Aayog? → Extra-constitutional body.
☛ Examples of extra-constitutional bodies? → National Human Rights Commission, Central Information Commission, Planning Commission.
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन एक अतिरिक्त संवैधानिक निकाय है? (RRB JE (26/05/2019) Shift 2 CBT 1)
options_hi: भाषा आयोग
चुनाव आयोग
वित्त आयोग
योजना आयोग
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है योजना आयोग

Explanation:
भारत में संवैधानिक निकाय वे होते हैं जिनका उल्लेख संविधान में स्पष्ट रूप से किया गया है, जैसे चुनाव आयोग (अनुच्छेद 324), वित्त आयोग (अनुच्छेद 280), और भाषा आयोग (अनुच्छेद 344)। योजना आयोग एक अतिरिक्त संवैधानिक निकाय था, जिसे 1950 में एक प्रस्ताव के माध्यम से स्थापित किया गया था, न कि संविधान के किसी प्रावधान के तहत। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य देश के आर्थिक विकास के लिए पंचवर्षीय योजनाएँ तैयार करना था। 2014 में इसे भंग कर नीति आयोग का गठन किया गया, जो भी एक अतिरिक्त संवैधानिक निकाय है। अतः सही उत्तर योजना आयोग है।

question: What does the Ashoka's wheel in the Indian National Flag represent? (RRB JE (26/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)
options: Wheel of peace
Wheel of prosperity
Wheel of the law of dharma
Wheel of authority
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Wheel of the law of dharma

Explanation:
The Ashoka Chakra in the Indian National Flag represents the Wheel of Law (Dharma Chakra). It is derived from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath. The chakra has 24 spokes, symbolizing 24 hours and the movement of life. It signifies justice, progress, and truth. The chakra is placed in the center of the white band of the flag in navy blue. The wheel implies dynamism and change, representing the nation's continuous progress. Although associated with Buddhism, in the national flag it stands for secularism and moral values. The chakra was adopted on 22 July 1947 during the Constituent Assembly session.

☛ On which band of the Indian flag is the Ashoka Chakra placed? → White band
☛ What is the colour of the Ashoka Chakra? → Navy blue
☛ When was the Ashoka Chakra incorporated into the Indian flag? → 22 July 1947

Explanation:
भारत के राष्ट्रीय ध्वज में अशोक चक्र धर्म के नियम (Wheel of Law) का प्रतीक है। यह चक्र सम्राट अशोक के सारनाथ स्तंभ से लिया गया है। इसमें 24 तीलियाँ होती हैं, जो 24 घंटे और जीवन की गति को दर्शाती हैं। अशोक चक्र न्याय, प्रगति और सत्य का प्रतीक है। यह ध्वज के सफेद पट्टी के बीच में नेवी ब्लू रंग में बना होता है। चक्र का अर्थ है गतिशीलता और परिवर्तन, जो देश की निरंतर प्रगति को दर्शाता है। यह धर्मचक्र बौद्ध धर्म से जुड़ा है, लेकिन राष्ट्रीय ध्वज में यह धर्मनिरपेक्षता और नैतिक मूल्यों का प्रतीक है।

question: Who has the power to proclaim the state of emergency in India? (RRB JE (27/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)
options: Vice-President
President
Prime Minister
Chief Justice of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
Under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to proclaim a state of emergency. A national emergency can be imposed when the security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. The President issues such a proclamation based on the recommendation of the Council of Ministers. The proclamation must be approved by both houses of Parliament within two months. So far, three national emergencies have been declared in India: in 1962, 1971, and 1975.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Effect of national emergency on Fundamental Rights? → They can be suspended under Articles 358 and 359
☛ During emergency, who can make laws on subjects in Union List? → Parliament
☛ Maximum duration of national emergency? → Indefinite, but requires parliamentary approval every 6 months
☛ When was the first national emergency declared in India? → 1962 (India-China war)
question_hi: भारत में आपातकालीन स्थिति की घोषणा करने की शक्ति किसके पास है? (RRB JE (27/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a routine session of the Indian Parliament? (RRB JE (27/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)
options: Summer Session
Budget Session
Winter Session
Monsoon Session
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Summer Session

Explanation:
The Indian Parliament has three routine sessions: Budget Session, Monsoon Session, and Winter Session. There is no official Summer Session. The Budget Session starts in January-February and continues till April, during which the Union Budget is presented. The Monsoon Session is held from July to August. The Winter Session is convened in November-December. Each session has designated days for government business, passing bills, and discussions. The term 'Summer Session' is not used in parliamentary calendar.

☛ When is the Budget Session held? → January-February to April
☛ Which months include the Monsoon Session? → July-August
☛ What is the timing of Winter Session? → November-December
☛ Which session is not a routine session? → Summer Session
question_hi: इनमें से कौन सा सत्र भारतीय संसद का नियमित सत्र नहीं है? (RRB JE (27/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)

question: Which of the following is dealt in Article 78 of the Constitution? (RRB JE (27/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)
options: President's power to send advisory messages to the Parliament
Emergency powers of the President
President's power to get information from the Council of Ministers
Prime Minister's duty regarding keeping the President informed about the government's decisions and policies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prime Minister's duty regarding keeping the President informed about the government's decisions and policies

Explanation:
Article 78 deals with the duties of the Prime Minister. It states that the Prime Minister shall keep the President informed about all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation. This article ensures coordination between the executive and the President under the parliamentary system. It also requires the Prime Minister to furnish such information as the President may call for. Article 78 is not about the President's emergency powers or his power to send messages; it specifically lays down the Prime Minister's duty to communicate. It is part of Part V of the Constitution dealing with the Union Executive.

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 78 प्रधानमंत्री के कर्तव्यों से संबंधित है। इसके तहत प्रधानमंत्री का यह कर्तव्य है कि वह राष्ट्रपति को सरकार के निर्णयों और नीतियों के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करता रहे। यह अनुच्छेद संसदीय शासन प्रणाली में कार्यपालिका और राष्ट्रपति के बीच समन्वय सुनिश्चित करता है। इसके अलावा, प्रधानमंत्री को राष्ट्रपति द्वारा पूछी गई किसी भी जानकारी को देने का भी दायित्व है। अनुच्छेद 78 राष्ट्रपति को सूचित रखने की व्यवस्था करता है, न कि उनकी आपातकालीन शक्तियों या संदेश भेजने की शक्ति से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद भारतीय संविधान के भाग V में आता है जो केंद्रीय कार्यपालिका से संबंधित है।

question: Which of these Indian Prime Ministers did NOT face the parliament? (RRB JE (27/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)
options: Morarji Desai
V.P. Singh
Chandrasekhar
Charan Singh
solution:

Explanation:

He is the only Indian PM who never faced the parliament because no session of parliament was held during his tenure. His government fell before he could prove his majority in the Lok Sabha. question: What is the total number of members nominated by the President to the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha? (RRB JE (28/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)
options: 12
18
14
16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 14

Explanation:
According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the President can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha. These members are persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields like literature, art, science, and social service. Additionally, under Article 331, the President can nominate 2 members from the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha if the community is not adequately represented. However, the 104th Constitutional Amendment (2020) abolished the reserved seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, but the President's power to nominate remains. Thus, the total nominated members are 12 (Rajya Sabha) + 2 (Lok Sabha) = 14.
question_hi: राष्ट्रपति द्वारा लोक सभा और राज्य सभा में मनोनीत सदस्यों की कुल संख्या कितनी है? (RRB JE (28/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)
options_hi: 12
18
14
16
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 14

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 80 के अनुसार, राष्ट्रपति राज्य सभा में 12 सदस्यों को मनोनीत कर सकते हैं। ये सदस्य साहित्य, कला, विज्ञान और समाज सेवा जैसे क्षेत्रों में विशेष ज्ञान या व्यावहारिक अनुभव रखने वाले होते हैं। इसके अलावा, अनुच्छेद 331 के तहत, राष्ट्रपति लोक सभा में एंग्लो-इंडियन समुदाय के 2 सदस्यों को मनोनीत कर सकते हैं, यदि उन्हें लगता है कि समुदाय का पर्याप्त प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं है। 104वें संविधान संशोधन (2020) के बाद, लोक सभा और राज्य विधानसभाओं में एंग्लो-इंडियन के लिए आरक्षित सीटें समाप्त कर दी गईं, लेकिन राष्ट्रपति द्वारा मनोनयन की शक्ति अब तक बनी हुई है। इस प्रकार कुल मनोनीत सदस्यों की संख्या 12 (राज्य सभा) + 2 (लोक सभा) = 14 है।

question: The Constitution of India came into force on ______?A. 26.01.1950B. 15.08.1947C. 22.08.1947D. 01.01.1950 (RRB NTPC Tier I (05/04/2016) Shift 1)

B

solution:

Explanation:
The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) made by the Indian National Congress in 1930. With its enforcement, India became a sovereign, democratic republic. This day is celebrated as Republic Day. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar played a key role in drafting the Constitution. The original Constitution had 395 articles and 8 schedules.

question: Find out the odd in relation to the Indian Parliament.A. Budget SessionB. Summer SessionC. Monsoon SessionD. Winter Session (RRB NTPC Tier I (05/04/2016) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:
The Indian Parliament holds three sessions every year: Budget Session, Monsoon Session, and Winter Session. There is no separate official session called 'Summer Session'. Although the Budget Session is sometimes informally referred to as the Summer Session, it is not an official designation. The Budget Session is held in February-March, the Monsoon Session in July-September, and the Winter Session in November-December. Therefore, 'Summer Session' is the odd one out as it is not an officially recognized session of the Parliament.

question: What is the 99th amendment of the constitution about?A. Starting GST in India.B. Establishment of National Judicial Appointments Commission.C. solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is B. Establishment of National Judicial Appointments Commission

Explanation:
The 99th amendment of the Indian Constitution was passed in 2014. Its main objective was to establish the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), a new body for appointing judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts. Previously, appointments were made under the collegium system. NJAC was to comprise the Chief Justice, two senior judges, the Union Law Minister, and two eminent persons. However, in 2015, the Supreme Court declared this amendment unconstitutional, thus restoring the collegium system.

question: What is the principle to be followed in a cooperative society?A. Multiple votesB. One man one voteC. No voteD. One share one vote (RRB NTPC Tier I (06/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: A
C
B
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is One man one vote

Explanation:
The core principle of a cooperative society is one member one vote. This ensures democratic control, where each member has equal voting rights regardless of the amount of capital or number of shares they hold. This distinguishes cooperatives from other business organizations like companies, where voting is based on shareholding. Multiple votes and one share one vote are against the cooperative principle. No vote is also incorrect because members must participate in decision-making. This principle is one of the cooperative principles recognized by the International Cooperative Alliance (ICA).

☛ Voting in cooperative society is based on → Membership, not shares

question: According to the Constitution of India, which one of the following is not a fundamental right?A. Right to freedomB. Right to liveC. Right to equalityD. Right to protect the country (RRB NTPC Tier I (07/04/2016) Shift 3)

Explanation:
Part 3 (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution enumerates the fundamental rights. question: In accordance with the Indian Constitution, Protection of Life and Personal Liberty is granted under which Article?A. Article 20B. Article 21C. Article 22D. Article 23 (RRB NTPC Tier I (16/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: D
C
B

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
Article 21 of the Indian Constitution provides protection of life and personal liberty. It states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This fundamental right has been interpreted broadly by the Supreme Court to include the right to live with dignity, right to privacy, right to a pollution-free environment, and many other essential rights. It is different from Article 20 (protection from conviction for offences), Article 22 (protection from arrest), and Article 23 (prohibition of human trafficking). Article 21 is considered the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution and is the most fundamental of all fundamental rights.

question: The annual financial statement prepared under article 112 of the Indian Constitution is called ______A. Public accountB. Consolidated accountC. BudgetD. Revenue account (RRB NTPC Tier I (19/04/2016) Shift 2)

question: _______ enacted during an emergency imposed by Mrs. Indira Gandhi, is also known as mini constitution because of important & large number of changes made to it.A. 42nd Amendment ActB. 44th Amendment ActC. 74th Amendment ActD. 73rd Amendment Act (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: D
A
C
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 42nd Amendment Act was passed in 1976 during the Emergency imposed by Mrs. Indira Gandhi in 1975. It is known as the 'Mini Constitution' because it made sweeping changes to many parts of the Indian Constitution. This amendment added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. It also introduced Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) and strengthened the powers of the central government. Additionally, it made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers. The 44th Amendment was passed in 1978 to undo the distortions caused during the Emergency. The 73rd and 74th Amendments relate to Panchayati Raj and Municipalities respectively.

question_hi: श्रीमती इंदिरा गांधी द्वारा लगाए गए आपातकाल के दौरान _______ को महत्वपूर्ण और बड़ी संख्या में किए गए परिवर्तनों के कारण मिनी संविधान के रूप में भी जाना जाता है।A. 42वां संशोधन अधिनियमB. 44वां संशोधन अधिनियमC. 74वाँ संशोधन अधिनियमD. 73वाँ संशोधन अधिनियम (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 1)
options_hi: D
A
C
B
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 42वां संशोधन अधिनियम

Explanation:
1975 में लगाए गए आपातकाल के दौरान 1976 में 42वां संशोधन अधिनियम पारित किया गया। इसे 'मिनी संविधान' कहा जाता है क्योंकि इसमें संविधान के कई भागों में बड़े पैमाने पर बदलाव किए गए। इस अधिनियम ने प्रस्तावना में 'समाजवादी', 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' और 'अखंडता' शब्द जोड़े। इसने नागरिकों के मूल कर्तव्यों को जोड़ा और केंद्र सरकार की शक्तियों को बढ़ाया। इसके अलावा, राष्ट्रपति के लिए मंत्रिमंडल की सलाह मानना अनिवार्य किया गया। 44वां संशोधन 1978 में आपातकाल के दुरुपयोग को सुधारने के लिए लाया गया था। 73वां और 74वां संशोधन पंचायती राज और नगरपालिकाओं से संबंधित हैं।
